log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Klefki + Rotom-Wash. Klefki sets Reflect (Prankster) to blunt physical rain sweepers; Rotom-Wash Volt Switch OHKOs Pelipper and Hydro Pump threatens Swampert. Turn 1 Whimsicott Encore on Klefki fails because Klefki hasn't moved yet. Back Incineroar for Intimidate cycling and Fake Out, Serperior as late-game Contrary sweeper after Fairy/Dragon threats are handled.

Pelipper sets Drizzle on lead to enable Swampert's Swift Swim (via Mega Evolution) and Basculegion/Pelipper water pressure, while Basculegion and Whimsicott backline provide clean-up speed control and power against the opponent's known roster (Serperior, Incineroar, Klefki, Rotom-Wash).
decisions.notebook: Game 2 team preview. Opponent runs Serperior, Incineroar, Klefki, Rotom-Wash based on Game 1.

decisions.rationale: Reflect (+1 Prankster) goes up before Swampert-Mega's Earthquake, halving it to ~28-42% on Klefki. Volt Switch OHKOs Pelipper through rain (132-261%); if Pelipper Protects, Volt Switch fails but Reflect is still up and rain setter is forced to Protect again or switch next turn. Speed tie between Rotom-Wash (116) and Pelipper (85-117) at priority 0 means Volt Switch may even deny Tailwind. This line secures early momentum: either Pelipper dies and we pivot into Incineroar for Intimidate, or Pelipper burns Protect and we have Reflect for the long game.

Klefki stays in (Pass) to continue setting screens or spreading paralysis with Prankster Thunder Wave. Rotom-Wash switches to Incineroar: switches resolve first, Intimidate immediately drops Swampert and the incoming replacement's Attack, and Incineroar threatens Fake Out next turn. Keeping Rotom-Wash healthy in back preserves its rain-boosted Hydro Pump and Volt Switch pivot for later. Serperior stays in reserve until Fairy/Dragon threats are scouted or removed.

Setting up Tailwind with Pelipper while Mega Swampert hits an Earthquake that deals heavy damage to Klefki (immune/levitate for Rotom means Rotom isn't hit by EQ) allows us to gain immediate speed control and pressure Klefki before it sets dual screens.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent's visible active Pokémon are Klefki and Rotom-Wash. Pelipper and Swampert lead.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper fainted last turn, so we must replace it. Bringing in Basculegion under Rain allows us to threaten strong Water/Ghost pressure alongside Mega Swampert. Swampert must pass its action since it cannot act independently when paired with a fainted slot being replaced.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent's active Pokémon are Klefki and Incineroar under Reflect and Rain. Sent in Basculegion for fainted Pelipper.

decisions.rationale: Thunder Wave onto Basculegion is the only speed-control answer to the Scarf Adaptability sweeper; Prankster guarantees it resolves before Wave Crash or Last Respects. Fake Out onto Swampert prevents Earthquake this turn regardless of Mega Evolution, buying a free turn. Worst case: Swampert Protects and Basculegion connects, but at least Basculegion is paralyzed for the rest of the game. Serperior remains in the back to clean after rain threats are weakened.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain: Pelipper (fainted), Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, +1 unrevealed (Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos). Whimsicott likely if they want Encore+Tailwind; Primarina/Ampharos if they fear Serperior. Keep Serperior healthy in back. Paralyze Basculegion and cycle Intimidate with Parting Shot to neutralize physical rain sweepers. Rotom-Wash is the Ground-immune pivot if Klefki goes down.

decisions.rationale: Klefki has only Pass/Forfeit options; we never forfeit up 1-0. Serperior is the clear switch: Leaf Storm OHKOs both Swampert-Mega (145-252%) and Basculegion (85-155%), resists both Water and Ground moves, and even if Swampert-Mega outspeeds with Swift Swim and lands Ice Punch (27-38%), Serperior survives and KOs back. Contrary also turns Leaf Storm into a snowball. Rotom-Wash is defensively solid but cannot threaten Swampert-Mega reliably (Hydro Pump 38-84%, Volt Switch immune).
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain: Pelipper (fainted), Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, +1 unrevealed (Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos). Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs both current foes. Keep Serperior healthy; it is the primary win condition against rain. Rotom-Wash is the Ground-immune pivot if Klefki goes down. Paralyzed Basculegion has 25% full-para chance each turn.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Basculegion) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Basculegion's Wave Crash cleanly KOs the weakened Incineroar (at 65% HP) through Reflect under Rain (with Choice Scarf and Adaptability), while Swampert Mega Evolves and uses Earthquake to hit both opponents (Klefki and Incineroar) for heavy damage while Swampert's Swift Swim activates next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Basculegion Choice Scarf outspeeds the board. Swampert Mega Evolving under rain grants Swift Swim for subsequent turns.

decisions.rationale: Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Basculegion through Choice lock (cannot Protect) before it moves, removing the Wave Crash threat. Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave paralyzes Swampert-Mega, halving its Speed and stripping Swift Swim for future turns while adding a 25% full-para chance this same turn. Swampert's attacks into Serperior are negligible (Ice Punch 27–39%, Earthquake 10–14%) under Reflect and -1 Atk. Next turn, a +2 SpA Serperior OHKOs the paralyzed Swampert, leaving only the unrevealed fourth Pokémon to handle with Serperior, Klefki, and full-HP Rotom-Wash.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent rain team is Pelipper (fainted), Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, plus one of Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos. Serperior is the primary win condition with Contrary Leaf Storm. Rotom-Wash is the Ground-immune pivot. Reflect has 6 turns remaining. Opponent's unrevealed fourth will appear after Basculegion faints.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion is Choice-locked into Wave Crash and facing Serperior (resistant) + Reflect. Switching Basculegion to Whimsicott preserves momentum, while Swampert Protects to scout Serperior's Leaf Storm/Dragon Pulse and stall Reflect/Rain turns.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Basculegion locked into Wave Crash. Swampert under Rain with Swift Swim.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Serperior)
decisions.rationale: Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert-Mega guaranteed (288-502%) and also OHKOs Basculegion if it switches in. Light Screen buffers against Whimsicott Moonblast and any special attacks from the back. Whimsicott's Prankster Encore is faster than Klefki, but if it Encores Serperior it locks the Leaf Storm I'm already using; if it Encores Klefki, Thunder Wave still provides value. Swampert-Mega's speed is uncertain vs Serperior (180-244 vs 181), but even if it Ice Punches first, Serperior survives (27-38.8%) and retaliates for the KO, reaching +4 SpA. The double-target risk (Ice Punch + Moonblast on Serperior) maxes at ~86% with Reflect, leaving Serperior alive to sweep.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent rain team is Pelipper (fainted), Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, Whimsicott. Serperior is the primary win condition with Contrary Leaf Storm. Rotom-Wash is the Ground-immune pivot. Reflect has 5 turns remaining after this turn. Light Screen will be up for 8 turns (Light Clay). Opponent's unrevealed fourth (Primarina or Ampharos) was not brought.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Protects to block any incoming attack (such as Klefki Thunder Wave / Foul Play or Serperior Leaf Storm) while Swampert-Mega uses Earthquake, which hits both Klefki and Serperior super-effectively/neutrally through Reflect (Klefki is weak to Ground, and Serperior takes heavy damage despite Reflect since Earthquake is physical and Swampert hits hard, or we can pick off Klefki). Wait, let's check Swampert's Earthquake damage or Encore options. Actually, Swampert's Earthquake hits Klefki (2x) and Serperior (0.5x), and Whimsicott protecting prevents friendly fire. Alternatively, Whimsicott Encores Serperior into Leaf Storm (if it used it) or Klefki into Thunder Wave. But Protect on Whimsicott is safe, and Earthquake breaks Klefki's Reflect / damages them both. Let's execute Protect + Earthquake.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Basculegion (252-461%) and boosts to +6 SpA via Contrary. Klefki Thunder Wave paralyzes Whimsicott for permanent speed control. Whimsicott's Prankster Encore/Tailwind goes first regardless, but locking Serperior into Leaf Storm is harmless when it's at +6 and the only remaining foe is a 37% Whimsicott with Sash. Basculegion Wave Crash can threaten Klefki (60-90%) but even if Klefki falls, +6 Serperior wins the 1v1 against paralyzed Whimsicott.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Serperior is the primary win condition with Contrary Leaf Storm. Rotom-Wash is the Ground-immune pivot, still at full HP in back. Opponent's rain team: Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, Whimsicott. After eliminating Basculegion, only Whimsicott remains. Reflect has 4 turns left, Light Screen 7 turns.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott uses Encore on Serperior (or Klefki if desired, but Encore on Serperior locks it into Leaf Storm or prevents it from pivoting safely if it protected) while Basculegion fires Wave Crash into Serperior to chip through screens or target Serperior.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Basculegion Choice Scarf locked into Wave Crash. Serperior +4 SpA.

decisions.rationale: Klefki is Encored into Light Screen which is already active and would fail; switching to Rotom-Wash escapes Encore and brings in a healthy pivot. Serperior's +6 Leaf Storm is a guaranteed KO on Whimsicott from 37% — Focus Sash leaves it at 1 HP, but Whimsicott is the opponent's last Pokémon and cannot OHKO Serperior through screens (Moonblast does 20–32%). Even if Whimsicott Protects, we repeat next turn with Rotom-Wash and Serperior both healthy behind dual screens.

Klefki is encored into Light Screen and will use Light Screen. Serperior is at +6 SpA and will attack. Whimsicott outspeeds Serperior and can use Moonblast into Klefki to chip it or into Serperior if appropriate; Klefki is vulnerable to Moonblast (though 0.5x, but Serperior resists or takes neutral? Wait, Serperior is Grass, Moonblast is Fairy, neutral). Actually, let's look at Moonblast into Serperior or Klefki. Moonblast into Serperior damages the dangerous threat at +6 SpA. Basculegion is fainted so its slot is pass.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Serperior reached +6 SpA; Klefki encored into Light Screen.

reflections.summary: Game 2 was won by a controlled Serperior sweep after an early KO on Pelipper removed Hurricane pressure and Klefki’s Thunder Wave paralyzed the Scarf Basculegion, preventing it from revenging. Screens enabled Serperior to stack Contrary boosts safely and overpower the entire rain squad. The series win resulted from correctly adjusting to a screen-supported Serperior plan, which the opponent lacked an answer for once Basculegion was disabled.
reflections.adjustment: The between-game adjustment to bring Serperior and Klefki over Mega Metagross and Corviknight was decisive; it exploited the opponent’s rain reliance perfectly. In a future rematch, I would keep the same core but consider slotting Mega Metagross over Incineroar if they start bringing Primarina or Ampharos, as Metagross handles Fairy/Electric types while still providing offensive pressure. Serperior remains the premier win condition, and Klefki + Rotom‑Wash form a resilient screens‑pivot backbone.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors a rain offense of Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Scarf Basculegion, and Whimsicott, leaving Primarina and Ampharos in the back. Pelipper carries Damp Rock and Tailwind; Swampert aims to spam rain‑boosted Earthquakes; Basculegion is their speed control with Wave Crash; Whimsicott has Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast, Focus Sash. They will often lead Pelipper + Swampert or Basculegion. Serperior sweeps their entire roster once screens are up and the opposing speed threats (Basculegion, Tailwind) are neutralized via Thunder Wave or an early KO. Paralyzing Basculegion is priority to block Aqua Jet/Last Respects. Rotom‑Wash is a reliable pivot to dispatch Pelipper and absorb Ground moves. In future series, expect they might bring Ampharos or Primarina to diversify, but Serperior still hits both super‑effectively; just be wary of Ampharos’s Static and Primarina’s Moonblast if screens are absent. Continue to lead Klefki + Rotom or Klefki + Incineroar for immediate disruption and pivot into Serperior for a safe setup sweep.

reflections.summary: You lost the series 0-2 because Serperior scaled out of control with Contrary Leaf Storm under dual screens and speed control disruption (Thunder Wave), while your aggressive rain offense was dismantled by Rotom-Wash pivoting, Incineroar's utility, and Klefki's support. The team-preview plan of bringing Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Whimsicott made sense on paper for a rain setup, but the lack of immediate special pressure allowed Serperior to boost freely and sweep.
reflections.adjustment: Against dual screen and Contrary setups like Serperior paired with Prankster Klefki, bring faster taunt or strong physical breakers that ignore screens or punch through them (such as Alakazam or heavier offensive pressure) rather than relying purely on speed-dependent rain sweepers that get crippled by Thunder Wave.
reflections.notebook: Serperior heavily exploits Contrary + Life Orb Leaf Storm once screens are up; Klefki provides reliable dual screens and Thunder Wave speed control; Rotom-Wash counters rain leads effectively with Volt Switch.
